key_insight: Daily remote monitoring with the standard QoR-15 survey is too burdensome for many patients, leading to poor adherence. The paper introduces QoR-compact to preserve recovery measurement while making patient reporting easier and more sustainable.
problem_solved: The study addresses the mismatch between QoR-15’s original use case (occasional in-hospital assessment) and its newer use in daily remote patient monitoring, where completion rates drop over time.
method: Analyze real-world post-surgical remote monitoring data to identify adherence problems with daily QoR-15 use.
Develop a shorter, more patient-friendly alternative called QoR-compact.
Optimize the survey for repeated remote use while preserving the subjective recovery signal needed for clinical monitoring.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights that model or system performance in healthcare depends not only on prediction quality but also on human data collection behavior. Better instrument design can improve data completeness, reduce burden, and make downstream monitoring systems more reliable.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of QoR-15 vs QoR-compact survey length
Line chart showing declining survey completion over 30 monitoring days
Patient monitoring workflow diagram from symptom reporting to recovery tracking
Icon set showing burden, adherence, and recovery signal quality
paper_title: AI-driven Optimisation of Quality of Recovery (QoR) in Remote Patient Monitoring
paper_authors: Yansong Liu,  Li-Hsi,  Lin, Pramit Khetrapal, Ronnie Stafford
